lines.text: Hundreds of islands in a turquoise sea, where Columbus first landed and pirates once ruled. This is the story of the Bahamas.
For centuries the Lucayan people lived here. Then in 1492 Columbus made landfall, and within a few years the Lucayans were carried off as slaves.
By the early seventeen hundreds, pirates ruled. The most feared of them, Blackbeard, used Nassau as his base.
Nassau, on New Providence, grew into the capital, and the British finally drove the pirates out.
Sidney Poitier, raised in the Bahamas, became the first Black man to win the Oscar for Best Actor.
Lynden Pindling was born. He would lead the islands to independence as their first prime minister.
Hubert Ingraham was born, a future prime minister of the nineties and two thousands.
Philip Davis was born, the man who would become prime minister of the Bahamas in 2021.
And Mychal Thompson, born in Nassau, became the first foreign-born player picked first in the NBA draft.
In 1973 the Bahamas became independent from Britain, a nation living from tourism and banking.
Shaunae Miller-Uibo was born. She would win Olympic gold over four hundred metres, twice.
In 2019 Hurricane Dorian stalled over the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama, leaving terrible destruction.
From the Lucayans to the present day, the Bahamas keep rebuilding with the tide.
